title: Generate and Use a GPG Key for Signed Git Commits
excerpt: Learn how to generate a GPG key and use it to sign your Git commits.
author: Alex Oluwaseyi
content:
### Generate GPG Key 🔑

To generate a new GPG key, run the following command:

```sh
gpg --gen-key
```

### Add GPG Key to Git Configuration 🔧

Once generated, set your GPG key ID in Git:

```sh
git config --global user.signingkey <gpg key id>
```

### Verify Your GPG Key ✅

Ensure your key exists by listing all available keys:

```sh
gpg --list-keys
```

### Export Public Key 📤

To use your key with GitHub, export your public key:

```sh
gpg --armor --export <gpg key id>
```

### Set Up GPG Key in GitHub 🔗

1. Sign in to [GitHub](https://github.com/settings/keys).
2. Click [New GPG Key](https://github.com/settings/gpg/new).
3. Copy and paste your public key from the previous step.

Example:

```C
-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----
random characters representing your public key
-----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----
```

### Enable Vigilant Mode 🛡

To ensure unsigned commits are flagged, enable `Vigilant Mode` by selecting `Flag unsigned commits as unverified` in GitHub settings.

### Start Signing Your Commits ✍️

To sign a commit, use the `-S` flag:

```sh
git commit -S -m "Your commit message"
```

To enable GPG signing for all future commits, run:

```sh
git config --global commit.gpgSign true
```

📝 Now, every commit you make will be GPG-signed! 🔐
